summary: Claim A cannot be sealed as preregistered, because one of its arms cannot legally be built under the campaign's own sub-bit law. This is a design collision, not a scheduling problem, and no amount of further packing resolves it.

preregistration.title: The iso-memory frontier and the RandomPolicy control

the_collision.requirement: Iso-memory means every arm spends the same physical bytes.
the_collision.measured: Uniform needs 2.53125 BPW to spend what the conditioned arms spend at ~1.0 with a natively carried embedding and head.
the_collision.evidence: PROMETHEUS_ARCHITECTURE.json:304 solved_main_bpw = 2.53125; HAWKING_MOTHERLOAD_REPORT.md:124 states the same figure and notes the four arms match to 0.0175 percent.
the_collision.conflict: BPW_CEILING is 1.0 and the sub-bit-first law is binding. An iso-memory Uniform arm at 2.53 BPW is 2.5x over that ceiling and may not be built without formally invoking the Escape Receipt -- a POLICY REVERSAL of the project's governing law, not an engineering choice.
the_collision.consequence: The two realized arms are also not comparable to each other: 0.9774 against 0.883 BPW is not iso-memory, so even a two-arm reading of the preregistration is unavailable.

what_this_is_not: This is NOT a null result. A null means the experiment ran and found no effect. This experiment cannot run as designed. Recording it as null would claim evidence that does not exist.

options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.option: Invoke the Escape Receipt for the Uniform arm
options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.cost: Reverses the sub-bit-first law for one arm. Requires explicit human authorization; the law was adopted deliberately and is enforced in code.
options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.note: Would make the preregistered design buildable exactly as filed.

options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.option: Redesign the comparison as iso-RATE rather than iso-memory
options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.cost: Every arm packs at the same BPW and spends different bytes. Answers a different and still useful question -- does conditioning beat uniform allocation at equal rate -- but it is not the filed preregistration and amending a preregistration after seeing results is exactly what preregistration exists to prevent.
options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.note: If taken, it must be filed as a NEW preregistration, not an edit of PROM-001.

options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.option: Seal PROM-001 as UNREALIZABLE_AS_FILED and proceed
options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.cost: Claim A contributes no evidence to the campaign.
options_none_of_which_are_the_controller.note: Honest, cheap, and preserves the record. This is the default if no authorization arrives.

current_disposition: Recorded as UNREALIZABLE_AS_FILED pending an explicit decision. The Continuum does not block on it: the six-gate pre-Odyssey amendment that HEAD adopted does not list Claim A as a gate, and HAWKING_ODYSSEY_READY is already sealed without it.
cost_if_pursued_anyway: Each missing arm is a full 282-shard pack plus source re-fetch. At the current measured rate that is hours per arm, and the Uniform arm remains illegal regardless of how long it is run.
not_evidence_of: any capability comparison between conditioned and uniform allocation -- that comparison has not been made
